newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products -- Gulf gasoline diffs rally.

text.p: U.S. Gulf gasoline differentials rallied on Monday in a bidding war among traders, while New York Harbor held much of its ground in quiet activity.
NYMEX prompt gasoline rose due to the continuing strength in the cash market and news the U.N. approved the Iraq aid plan did little to deflate gains.
NYMEX September gasoline was up 0.73 cents at 65.80 cents a gallon, with August heat down 0.1 cent at 56.55 cents a gallon. September crude was down 13 cents at $20.15 a barrel.
U.S. GULF

Gulf Coast nearby conventional M1 gasoline differentials skyrocketed once again as buyers competed to secure barrels for delivery on the front 23d cycle on the Colonial Pipeline. That cycle reaches a scheduling deadline on Wednesday.
Coventional M1 gasoline for the front 23d moved to about 3.00 cents over the September NYMEX price after starting the morning at about 1.00 cent over the screen.
"There's been a lot traders buying here today," one Gulf player said.
Differentials for the back 22d cycle on the Colonial reached a high of 4.00 cents over the September futures on Friday before hitting the scheduling deadline at the end of the day.
Prompt premium conventional V1 gasoline also firmed Monday as quotes for prompt barrels reached an 8.00-cent premium to the conventional M1 grade.
NEW YORK HARBOR

New York Harbor prompt conventional unleaded gasoline was slightly stronger, but trade Monday midday was quiet. Differentials were pegged at 2.50/2.70 cents over the September screen with the any months at a penny under.

Prompt A2 reformulated northern-grade gasoline eased, with a deal heard done at 7.00 cents over the September print. High prices of the gasoline additive MTBE, tight supply and a wide Sept-Oct spread has kept underlying support for A2. Barrels delivered by August 10th were pegged at 5.75 cents.
The 93-octane premium and the 93-octane reformulated grades were notional due to the quiet activity.
Distillates were pegged steady to weaker, with prompt low sulphur diesel weaker at 0.75/1.00 over the print.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent gasoline markets shed some of last week's strength due to a sharp drop off in demand.
Group Three unleaded, which firmed more than two cents last week, fell a half cent to 5.50/6.00 cents. A deal for 5.85 cent over the print was done.
Chicago unleaded differentials also fell a half cent to be even with Group Three. Third cycle barrels were offered at 3.00 cents over the screen.
Group Three low sulphur diesel dipped a quarter cent to 2.00/2.25 for prompt barrels. Chicago material fell about a cent to 1.25/1.50 cents below the screen.
-- New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
